new_pattern_hanzi: 地名 + 在 + 哪儿？
old_teaching_note: Ask for a location with 在哪儿 (zài nǎr), without adding 吗 (ma).
new_teaching_note: Replace the place name to ask about a street, building, or meeting point.

new_pattern_hanzi: 不在 + 地点
old_teaching_note: Negate a location with 不在 (bú zài); the 不 changes tone before fourth-tone 在.
new_teaching_note: After correcting a mistaken location, give the right place or direction.

new_pattern_hanzi: 喝 + 饮料 + 还是 + 饮料？
old_teaching_note: 还是 (háishi) is normal in questions that present a choice.
new_teaching_note: The speaker is asking the listener to select one of the drinks.

new_pattern_hanzi: 动词 + 名词 + 或者 + 名词
old_teaching_note: 或者 (huòzhě) commonly offers alternatives in statements.
new_teaching_note: This describes possibilities instead of directly requesting a choice.

new_pattern_hanzi: 现在 + 几点钟？
old_teaching_note: 几点钟 (jǐ diǎn zhōng) asks for a clock time, not a duration.
new_teaching_note: Ask for the current clock time before arranging a meeting.

new_pattern_hanzi: 时间 + 不行
old_teaching_note: Suggest a time with 好吗 (hǎo ma); reject an unsuitable time with 不行 (bù xíng).
new_teaching_note: Give an alternative time after declining the first suggestion.

new_pattern_hanzi: 时间 + 不行；另一个时间 + 可以
new_pattern_pinyin: shíjiān + bù xíng; lìng yí ge shíjiān + kěyǐ
old_teaching_note: 不行 (bù xíng) rejects a proposal; 可以 (kěyǐ) accepts an alternative.
new_teaching_note: This keeps negotiations moving by supplying an acceptable alternative.

new_pattern_hanzi: 太 + 形容词 + 了
old_teaching_note: 太 (tài) + adjective + 了 (le) expresses an excessive degree or a strong judgment.
new_teaching_note: In scheduling, it explains why a proposed time is unsuitable.

new_pattern_hanzi: 想喝 + 饮料 + 还是 + 饮料？
old_teaching_note: Use 还是 (háishi) to present alternatives in a question.
new_teaching_note: Offer two drinks and let the listener choose one.

new_pattern_hanzi: 数量 + 杯 + 饮料
old_teaching_note: 杯 (bēi) counts cups or glasses of drinks.
new_teaching_note: Use the classifier when ordering a specific number of cups.

new_pattern_hanzi: 陈述句 + 吗？
old_teaching_note: The neutral-tone question particle 吗 (ma) can form a yes–no question.
new_teaching_note: This example is a friendly check on how the other person is doing.

new_pattern_hanzi: 请问 + 问题
old_teaching_note: A polite way to introduce a request for information.
new_teaching_note: Use this opener when politely approaching someone you do not know.

new_pattern_hanzi: 物品 + 多少钱？
old_teaching_note: 多少钱 (duōshao qián) asks for the price.
new_teaching_note: Name the item when checking a quoted price.

new_pattern_hanzi: 数量 + 块 + 人民币
old_teaching_note: 块 (kuài) is the colloquial unit used to count yuan or a currency amount.
new_teaching_note: In ordinary conversations, 块 (kuài) is the casual word for yuan.

new_pattern_hanzi: 只有 + 数量 + 钱；不够
new_pattern_pinyin: zhǐ yǒu + shùliàng + qián; bú gòu
old_teaching_note: 只有 (zhǐ yǒu) emphasizes a limited amount; 够 (gòu) means enough.
new_teaching_note: This gives a practical reason for being unable to pay the requested amount.

new_pattern_hanzi: 有没有 + 物品？
old_teaching_note: 有没有 (yǒu méi yǒu) is the A-not-A form of 有 (yǒu), used for availability or possession.
new_teaching_note: Replace newspaper with another item when asking whether it is in stock.

new_pattern_hanzi: 物品 + 是不是 + 价格？
old_teaching_note: 是不是 (shì bú shì) asks for confirmation without a final 吗 (ma).
new_teaching_note: Use this to check the amount you think you heard.

new_pattern_hanzi: 数字 + 不是 + 另一个数字
new_pattern_pinyin: shùzì + bú shì + lìng yí ge shùzì
old_teaching_note: Check numbers carefully: 八 (bā) is eight, whereas 十八 (shíbā) is eighteen.
new_teaching_note: Repeat the corrected number if the buyer misheard the price.

new_pattern_hanzi: 数字 + 加 + 数字 + 是多少？
old_teaching_note: Use 加 (jiā) for addition; 多少 (duōshao) asks for the result.
new_teaching_note: Use the pattern to ask for a total during a purchase.

new_pattern_hanzi: 数字 + 十 + 数字
old_teaching_note: Numbers 11–19 use ten plus a digit, while 20–99 use tens plus a digit.
new_teaching_note: 二十五 (èrshíwǔ) consists of two tens plus five.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 是 + 身份
old_teaching_note: Use 是 (shì) to identify nationality or identity.
new_teaching_note: Replace the nationality with another identity to introduce yourself or someone else.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 不是 + 身份
old_teaching_note: 不 (bù) changes to bú before a fourth-tone syllable, as in 是 (shì).
new_teaching_note: The spoken reading changes to bú shì before fourth-tone 是 (shì).

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 是不是 + 身份？
old_teaching_note: 是不是 (shì bú shì) is a positive-negative question; normally omit final 吗 (ma) here.
new_teaching_note: A direct response may begin with 是 (shì) or 不是 (bú shì).

new_pattern_hanzi: 可不可以 + 动作？
old_teaching_note: An A-not-A form of 可以 (kěyǐ) asks about possibility or permission.
new_teaching_note: Ask whether an action is possible or allowed in the situation.

new_pattern_hanzi: 给 + 人 + 数量 + 物品
old_teaching_note: 给 (gěi) can mean to give something to someone.
new_teaching_note: In a polite request, consider adding 请 (qǐng) before the verb.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 可不可以 + 动词 + 物品？
new_pattern_pinyin: zhǔyǔ + kě bù kěyǐ + dòngcí + wùpǐn?
old_teaching_note: 可不可以 (kě bù kěyǐ) asks for permission or possibility as an A-not-A question.
new_teaching_note: Here the customer is checking whether paying in US dollars is acceptable.

new_pattern_hanzi: 请问 + 称呼 + 在吗？
old_teaching_note: Use 请问 (qǐngwèn) plus a name and 在吗 (zài ma) when asking if someone is available on the telephone.
new_teaching_note: This sounds courteous when another person answers the telephone.

new_pattern_hanzi: 时间 + 不行；另一个时间 + 呢？
new_pattern_pinyin: shíjiān + bù xíng; lìng yí ge shíjiān + ne?
old_teaching_note: The particle 呢 (ne) offers an elliptical alternative when the topic is already understood.
new_teaching_note: The follow-up invites the other speaker to consider another time.

new_pattern_hanzi: 太晚了 + 早点见
new_pattern_pinyin: tài wǎn le + zǎo diǎn jiàn
old_teaching_note: Use 太晚了 (tài wǎn le) to object and 早点 (zǎo diǎn) to suggest an earlier time.
new_teaching_note: Pair your objection with a concrete earlier meeting suggestion.

new_pattern_hanzi: 想 + 去 + 地点 + 动作
old_teaching_note: Combine destination and purpose in one sentence.
new_teaching_note: Link a proposed destination to the activity you want to do there.

new_pattern_hanzi: 在 + 地点 + 动作
old_teaching_note: Use 在 (zài) before a place to say where an action happens.
new_teaching_note: You can use this structure to suggest staying here instead of going elsewhere.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 会 + 说 + 语言
old_teaching_note: 会 (huì) expresses acquired ability; add a language after 说 (shuō).
new_teaching_note: Use this to describe a language you can speak, even if your ability is limited.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 说 + 得 + 程度
old_teaching_note: 得 (de) introduces how well the action is performed.
new_teaching_note: This form can compliment someone on how well they speak a language.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 说得 + 不太好
new_pattern_pinyin: zhǔyǔ + shuō de + bú tài hǎo
old_teaching_note: The result complement 得 (de) describes how well an action is performed; do not confuse it with 的 (de).
new_teaching_note: A modest reply acknowledges limited ability without claiming you cannot speak at all.

new_pattern_hanzi: 可是 + 对比的句子
old_teaching_note: 可是 (kěshì) introduces a contrast; 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr) has optional northern rhotic pronunciation.
new_teaching_note: The speaker contrasts one limitation with something they can still do.

new_pattern_hanzi: 时间词 + 主语 + 动词
old_teaching_note: Time words often precede the main verb or follow the topic.
new_teaching_note: Mentioning tomorrow first highlights when the planned action will happen.

new_pattern_hanzi: 过 + 一会儿 + 动词
old_teaching_note: This phrase means after a short while; 一 (yī) is pronounced yí before fourth-tone 会 (huì).
new_teaching_note: Use this when proposing to meet shortly rather than immediately.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 不 + 心理动词
old_teaching_note: Negate a mental state using 不 (bù); the next syllable is not fourth tone here.
new_teaching_note: This is a natural way to signal difficulty following what someone says.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 说 + 什么？
old_teaching_note: 什么 (shénme) occupies the position of the unknown thing in the sentence.
new_teaching_note: In a conversation, this asks the other person to clarify their words.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 想 + 动作
old_teaching_note: 想 (xiǎng) expresses a wish or desire followed by a verb.
new_teaching_note: A useful opening when suggesting what to eat or do next.

new_pattern_hanzi: 想不想 + 动作？
old_teaching_note: An A-not-A question asks whether someone wants to do something.
new_teaching_note: The listener can answer 想 (xiǎng) or 不想 (bù xiǎng).

new_pattern_hanzi: 跟 + 人 + 一起 + 动作
old_teaching_note: 跟 (gēn) introduces the person accompanying you; 一起 (yìqǐ) means together.
new_teaching_note: Use this when inviting someone to share a meal or activity.

new_pattern_hanzi: 主语 + 也 + 想 + 动作
old_teaching_note: 也 (yě) adds agreement or another participant doing the same thing.
new_teaching_note: A friendly response when you want to join someone else’s plan.
